studies.design: Participant-blinded randomized experiment, within-physician adversarial vs aligned AI
studies.ai_system: Conversational LLM assistant instructed to steer toward harmful (adversarial) or correct (aligned) options
studies.humans: Physicians from 42 countries and eight disciplines with neurocritical care expertise
studies.finding: Physicians made sequential diagnostic and treatment decisions on neurocritical care cases with AI assistance. Adversarial AI raised the harmful-decision rate from 2% with aligned AI to 49% (adjusted difference 47 percentage points, 95% CI, 43-51) and reduced the correct-decision rate from 83% to 25%, with no clear protection from experience. 141 of 190 physicians who made harmful decisions reported nothing unusual.
studies.limitation: Simulated anonymized cases in an experimental setting rather than live care; preprint not peer reviewed.
studies.title: Subversion of clinical judgment by conversational artificial intelligence

studies.design: Randomised equivalence trial
studies.finding: 130 adults undergoing elective surgery were randomised to the PEAR conversational AI before clinician contact or to standard preoperative consultation for education on anaesthesia risk. Post-consultation understanding scores in the PEAR group met the pre-specified equivalence criterion across all three primary measures. PEAR also reduced documentation and consultation time.
studies.limitation: Single-centre trial using patient-reported understanding; preprint, not peer reviewed.
studies.title: Randomised Trial of a Multilingual Conversational AI for Preoperative Education

studies.design: Secondary analysis of a cluster-randomised trial
studies.ai_system: AI Consult GenAI clinical decision support tool
studies.finding: Learning effects were examined in primary care clinicians with and without access to AI Consult, which flags risks of harm in documented decisions. Over several months, clinicians with access produced fewer red flags (14% reduction, p = 0.032 vs control 6% increase, p = 0.383). They also produced fewer yellow flags (6.8% reduction, p = 0.005 vs control 3% increase, p = 0.231).
studies.limitation: Outcome is the tool's own flag rates rather than patient outcomes; number of clinicians not stated; preprint.
studies.title: Learning Effects from A GenAI-based Clinical Decision Support System in Primary Healthcare

studies.design: Two large-scale experiments with lay people and primary care physicians using AI assistance with different XAI explanations
studies.ai_system: Fairness-based dermatology diagnosis AI with XAI explanations including multimodal LLM explanations
studies.finding: Skin condition diagnosis with AI assistance. AI assistance improved accuracy and reduced diagnostic disparities; PCPs benefited irrespective of AI accuracy with LLM explanations, while lay users showed automation bias. Presenting AI suggestions first led to worse outcomes when the AI was incorrect for both groups.
studies.limitation: Preprint; experimental setting and no numeric effect sizes in abstract.
studies.title: Explainable AI as a Double-Edged Sword in Dermatology: The Impact on Clinicians versus The Public

studies.design: Three identical randomized controlled trials in Indonesia, Kenya and the Netherlands using primary care vignettes
studies.finding: Clinical reasoning quality on vignettes with vs without LLM access. Diagnostic scores improved in Indonesia (b=7.9%) and Kenya (b=15.1%) but not the Netherlands (b=1.4%); management scores improved in all (Indonesia b=15.7%, Kenya b=27.3%, Netherlands b=12.3%).
studies.limitation: Preprint; simulated vignettes rather than live care.
studies.title: How Large Language Models Can Affect Clinical Reasoning: A Randomized Clinical Trial

studies.design: Single-center randomized crossover trial
studies.finding: Study days were randomized to AI-assisted or manual echocardiography workflow across 585 patients. AI reduced examination time (13.0 vs 14.3 minutes, p<0.001) and increased daily examinations (16.7 vs 14.1, p=0.003), with lower mental fatigue (4.1 vs 4.7, p=0.039) and improved image quality (p<0.001).
studies.limitation: Preprint; single center with only four sonographers.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence-based Automated Echocardiographic Analysis and the Workflow of Sonographers: A randomized crossover trial

studies.design: Randomized double-blind trial
studies.finding: Participants answered four clinical cases with four questions each using MedSearch or traditional search (Google, PubMed). The MedSearch group reached a final answer in half the time (three minutes faster) with approximately 66% fewer searches per case, with differences significant in all evaluated aspects (p <0.01).
studies.limitation: Preprint; most participants were medical students and cases were simulated.
studies.title: Real-world Validation of MedSearch: a conversational agent for real-time, evidence-based medical question-answering.

studies.design: Pragmatic cluster randomized controlled trial
studies.ai_system: AI-based predictive analytics risk trajectory display
studies.finding: 10,422 inpatient visits on a cardiology ward were randomised to a display of AI risk trajectories or usual care. There was no change in the primary outcome of clinical deterioration events between groups, and mortality was not reduced.
studies.limitation: 11% of patients moved between display and non-display beds, undermining randomisation; single site; preprint.
studies.title: A pragmatic randomized controlled trial of artificial intelligence (AI)-based predictive analytics monitoring for early detection of clinical deterioration

studies.design: Model development with external validation plus four-phase reader study including randomised phase
studies.ai_system: Ensemble of three deep learning ECG image models with Grad-CAM
studies.humans: 70 healthcare providers including cardiologists and non-cardiologists
studies.finding: For differentiating Takotsubo syndrome from anterior STEMI on ECG, readers' estimated probability of correct diagnosis rose from 0.632 unaided to 0.864 with AI assistance (OR 3.71); in the randomised phase AI improved accuracy vs reference sheet (OR 4.28) and Grad-CAM added benefit (OR 1.53). AI-assisted readers remained less accurate overall than the model alone.
studies.limitation: Retrospective ECG image set from two hospitals; reader study not in live care; subgroup analyses exploratory; preprint.
studies.title: Deep learning-based electrocardiographic differentiation of Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior myocardial infarction: explainability, human-AI interaction, and a utilization bias hypothesis

studies.design: Multicentre open-label randomised controlled trial with vignettes
studies.ai_system: Prof. Valmed certified LLM-based clinical decision support system
studies.humans: Physicians from seven hospitals in two countries
studies.finding: Physicians assessed three rheumatology vignettes before and after assistance. Top-1 accuracy increased from 22.2% to 33.3% with the LLM and from 23.3% to 35.0% with conventional resources (adjusted OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.45 to 2.19; p=0.979). Assisted case-processing time was shorter with LLM support (94 vs 206 s), and exploratory analyses showed substantial AI over-reliance.
studies.limitation: Preprint; only three vignettes rather than real patients.
studies.title: Certified large language model-based diagnostic decision support in rheumatology: the ALLIANCE multicentre randomised controlled trial

studies.design: Prospective multinational randomised controlled reader study
studies.ai_system: AI intracranial aneurysm detection flags on TOF-MRA
studies.humans: Radiology residents, general radiologists/fellows and neuroradiologists
studies.finding: Readers evaluating 20 TOF-MRA studies with AI flags (90% false-positive) were randomised to a 3-minute false positive paradox video or control. Acceptance of AI false positives was 12.7% in the intervention group vs 22.5% in controls (OR 0.50, one-sided p = 0.017), and follow-up was recommended in 39.2% vs 54.9% of cases.
studies.limitation: Preprint; artificial case mix with 90% false-positive flags and only 20 cases.
studies.title: A 3-Minute Education on the False Positive Paradox Improves Trust Calibration in AI-Assisted Intracranial Aneurysm Detection: A Multinational Randomized Controlled Reader Study

studies.design: Randomized vignette experiment
studies.finding: Physicians answered simulated clinical case questions with system support or usual search. Supported physicians scored higher on composite validity (medians 2.83 versus 2.46; difference 0.38; 95% CI 0.17 to 0.54) and were more likely to meet the validity threshold (odds ratio 3.61; 95% CI 1.16 to 11.17), but accuracy alone did not differ significantly.
studies.limitation: High attrition (71 of 202 analyzed), volunteer sample and post hoc choice of composite outcome make findings exploratory; preprint.
studies.title: Quality of physicians responses using a conversational artificial intelligence system: a randomized vignette experiment in Latin America

studies.design: Randomized controlled trial of a behavioral nudge during LLM-assisted vignette diagnosis
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT-5.1 with accuracy anchoring and traffic-light confidence nudge
studies.finding: Seventy-two physicians evaluated six vignettes with ChatGPT-5.1 recommendations, three containing deliberate clinically significant errors; the treatment arm received a dual-component nudge. Diagnostic reasoning scores were significantly higher in the nudge group than controls seeing recommendations alone (mean difference, 7.6 percentage-points; 95% CI, 1.4-13.9; P=0.016).
studies.limitation: Vignette-based with only six cases; compares two AI interface designs rather than AI vs no AI; preprint.
studies.title: Mitigating Automation Bias in Physician-LLM Diagnostic Reasoning Using Behavioral Nudges: A Randomized Controlled Trial

studies.design: Online randomized study of Basic vs Enhanced AI-CDSS interface; annotation alone then with AI
studies.ai_system: AI-CDSS outlining the sella on pituitary surgery video
studies.finding: Clinicians annotated the sella on six operative video clips first alone and then with an optional AI-CDSS, randomized to Basic or Enhanced interfaces. User performance (DICE) improved with the AI-CDSS, with no significant difference between groups on best or worst AI clips. When AI performed worst, trust was lower in the Enhanced group (3.00 vs 3.67, p=.035) and dispersion was less (IQR: 0.07 vs 0.21, p=.004).
studies.limitation: Online video annotation task rather than live surgery; 64 of 70 completed; preprint.
studies.title: Calibrating trust in AI-assisted pituitary surgery

studies.design: Deployment at two Nigerian outpatient clinics comparing unassisted and LLM-revised care plans, with blinded randomized on-site physician assessment, laboratory testing and retrospective academic review
studies.ai_system: LLM decision support giving feedback on care plans
studies.finding: Health workers drafted care plans and optionally revised them after LLM feedback, changing prescribing for more than half of patients. Retrospective academic reviewers rated LLM-assisted plans more favorably, but on-site physicians observed little to no improvement in diagnostic alignment or treatment decisions. Laboratory testing showed mixed effects, with no significant increase in detection rates for the tested conditions.
studies.limitation: Preprint from two clinics; the abstract gives no quantitative effect sizes or participant numbers.
studies.title: Can LLMs Improve Healthcare Delivery? Evidence from Physician Review and Objective Testing

studies.design: Prospective trial of real-time cholangioscopy AI in 41 patients, with secondary comparison against human observers reviewing footage
studies.finding: Classifying biliary strictures as benign or malignant. AI accuracy was 87.8% versus 61.5% for junior-level (p = 0.001) and 63.15% for experienced endoscopists (p = 0.011).
studies.limitation: Preprint, small sample of 41 patients; human comparison was a secondary outcome with unstated number of observers.
studies.title: The SMART-AI trial: Real-time cholangioscopy artificial intelligence for the classification of biliary strictures

studies.design: Prospective observational study in two ICUs comparing intensivist predictions with a machine learning model
studies.finding: Predicting intubation within 24 hours across 302 surveys. Sensitivity was 0.190 for physicians and 0.714 for Vent.io; specificity was 0.960 and 0.673 respectively.
studies.limitation: Preprint; two ICUs only, number of physicians not stated.
studies.title: Physician gestalt compared with AI model to predict intubation in critically ill patients

studies.design: Single-blind randomized controlled trial after 20-hour AI-literacy training
studies.finding: Physicians reviewed up to 6 clinical vignettes and were scored on diagnostic reasoning. Those with LLM access scored 71.4% versus 42.6% with conventional resources (adjusted difference 27.5 percentage points, 95% CI 22.8 to 32.2), with similar time per case (603.8 vs. 635 seconds). LLM alone outperformed the trained physician group by 11.5 percentage points.
studies.limitation: Preprint; vignette-based rather than real patients, and all participants received AI-literacy training, limiting generalisability.
studies.title: AI-literacy training enhances physician-LLM diagnostic collaboration in a resource-limited setting: a randomized controlled trial

studies.design: Single-center randomized controlled trial
studies.ai_system: Deep learning-enabled personal ultrasound device with real-time guidance
studies.humans: Internal medicine residents without sonography training
studies.finding: 38 residents received ultrasound devices with (N=19) or without (N=19) DL guidance for two weeks. At follow-up the DL group had faster five-view scan times (152 seconds [IQR 115-195] vs. 266 seconds [IQR 206-324]; p<0.001) and higher RACE image quality scores (15 [IQR 10-18] vs. 11 [IQR 7-13.5]; p=0.034).
studies.limitation: Preprint; small single-center trial with outcomes measured on a standardized patient.
studies.title: Limited Echocardiogram Acquisition by Clinicians Aided with Deep Learning: A Randomized Controlled Trial

studies.design: Observational study with retrospective and prospective phases
studies.finding: For detecting malignancy in suspicious skin lesions retrospectively, the device had an AUC of 0.76 versus 0.79 for dermatologists, with top-1 accuracy 0.23 versus 0.33. Prospectively, dermatologists assisted by the device, the device alone and the latest version achieved AUCs of 0.94, 0.95 and 0.97, and top-1 accuracies of 0.30, 0.22 and 0.26.
studies.limitation: Single centre, small samples (88 retrospective and 42 prospective lesions), no unassisted dermatologist arm in the prospective phase; preprint.
studies.title: Diagnostic accuracy in detecting malignancy in suspicious skin lesions using Artificial Intelligence

studies.design: Prospective international multicenter diagnostic study vs frozen section
studies.ai_system: RapidLymphoma (deep learning on stimulated Raman histology)
studies.finding: In a prospective cohort (n=160), RapidLymphoma achieved balanced accuracy of 97.81% and was non-inferior to frozen section analysis in detecting PCNSL (100% vs. 78.94%).
studies.limitation: Preprint; comparator is frozen section workflow, number of pathologists not stated.
studies.title: Fast intraoperative detection of primary CNS lymphoma and differentiation from common CNS tumors using stimulated Raman histology and deep learning

studies.design: Prospective comparative diagnostic study, single hospital
studies.ai_system: Object detection-based deep learning guidance for point-of-care ultrasound
studies.humans: 10 registered nurses with no ultrasonography experience using DL guidance vs physicians scanning without guidance
studies.finding: AAA screening with point-of-care ultrasound in 184 patients. DL-guided novice nurses achieved adequate scan quality in 87.5% (95% CI: 82.7 - 92.3%) of patients, comparable to 91.3% (95% CI: 87.2-95.4%) for physician scans (p=0.310). The DL model predicted AAA with an AUC of 0.975.
studies.limitation: Preprint; single center; compares AI-guided nurses with unaided physicians rather than same users with vs without AI; only 3 AAA cases.
studies.title: Prospective Clinical Evaluation of a Deep Learning Algorithm for Guided Point-of-Care Ultrasonography Screening of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms

studies.design: Prospective diagnostic accuracy study on video recordings against neurologist consensus
studies.ai_system: APOLLAI multimodal (computer vision, audio deep learning, SVM fusion)
studies.humans: EMS personnel (mean of 15 raters per patient)
studies.finding: Detecting five NIHSS-item deficits in 295 suspected stroke patients, APOLLAI had higher global sensitivity than EMS (78.5% versus 59.4%) with broadly comparable specificity (87.0% versus 85.9%). Global AUC was 0.882.
studies.limitation: Single centre, assessments from recorded videos rather than live prehospital conditions; preprint.
studies.title: APOLLAI, a multimodal AI system, versus EMS personnel for prehospital detection of stroke-related deficits

studies.design: Prospective diagnostic accuracy study of community screening and facility triage cohorts in South Africa, chest radiographs read by blinded human readers and CAD
studies.finding: Detection of microbiologically-confirmed asymptomatic TB on digital chest radiographs from 1,353 participants. For asymptomatic TB in the Screening Cohort, human reader sensitivity was 56.4% with specificity 94.1%, against qXR CAD sensitivity 69.2% with specificity 89.3%. The CAD minus human difference was 12.8% (95%CI -0.48 to 26.1) for sensitivity and -4.8% (95%CI -12.4 to 28.2) for specificity.
studies.limitation: Preprint, not peer reviewed. Only 39 asymptomatic TB cases, so confidence intervals are wide. The number of human readers is not stated.
studies.title: Performance of Human and Computer-aided Evaluation of Digital Chest Radiography for Community-based Screening of Asymptomatic Tuberculosis

studies.design: Model development with randomized crossover reader study of AI-assisted vs unassisted review
studies.finding: Pathologists graded gastric biopsies with the Updated Sydney System with and without SydneyMTL assistance in a randomized crossover reader study. AI-assisted review significantly reduced interpretation time and improved inter-observer agreement; no numeric results for the reader study are given in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Preprint; reader study results reported without numbers or reader count, and diagnostic accuracy with assistance not reported.
studies.title: SydneyMTL: Interpretable Multi-Task Learning for Complete Sydney System Assessment in Gastric Biopsies

studies.design: Randomized crossover preclinical trial in high-fidelity simulated surgery
studies.ai_system: Real-time computer vision AI-assisted navigation system
studies.finding: Nineteen neurosurgeons performed simulated pituitary tumour resections with and without AI assistance. AI assistance significantly improved technical performance (OSATS 19.79±4.06 vs. 17.32±4.11; p=0.027), especially for trainees (19.20±3.76 vs. 16.60±3.78), while expert performance remained stable. Subjective workload was higher with AI (SURG-TLX 26.42±9.56 vs. 22.26±7.81; p=0.014).
studies.limitation: Simulated surgery with small sample (19 surgeons, 4 experts); preprint.
studies.title: Real-time Computer Vision Assisted Navigation for Endoscopic Pituitary Surgery: Iterative Development and Comparative Preclinical Evaluation

studies.design: Randomized experiment comparing LLM explanation formats vs no support
studies.finding: Radiologists reviewed cases with radiological images (N = 2020 assessments) without LLM support or with one of three LLM explanation formats. Chain-of-thought explanations improved diagnostic accuracy by 12.2% versus no LLM support (P = 0.001), and outperformed standard output (+7.2%; P = 0.040) and differential diagnosis format (+9.7%; P = 0.004).
studies.limitation: Preprint; number of radiologists not stated and cases reviewed in an experimental rather than clinical setting.
studies.title: The effect of medical explanations from large language models on diagnostic decisions in radiology

studies.design: Retrospective in-silico vignette study, two-stage (pre/post biomarker) protocol
studies.finding: On six sepsis vignettes, model accuracy before biomarkers ranged 40-67%, comparable to physicians (57%). After biomarker disclosure physician accuracy was 61%, exceeded by Qwen3.8-27B (91%), its quantised variant (86%) and Gemma-4-31B (83%); DeepSeek-4 reached 64% and MedGemma 56%.
studies.limitation: Only six vignettes; simulated setting; preprint.
studies.title: Can Language Models Diagnose Sepsis? A Head-to-Head Evaluation Against 353 Physicians

studies.design: Prospective validation with fixed-order two-round reader study (unaided then AI-assisted after washout)
studies.ai_system: Interpretable deep learning classifier for digital tissue-based neural autoantibody assay images
studies.humans: Two expert and two novice readers
studies.finding: On 200 prospective tissue-based assay images, the standalone classifier achieved AUC 0.922 and accuracy of 86.5%. Pooled reader accuracy rose from 90.4% unaided to 97.4% with AI assistance (McNemar P < 0.001); novice accuracy rose from 83.3% to 96.5%, approaching unaided expert accuracy of 97.5%.
studies.limitation: Only four readers in a fixed-order, non-randomised design at a single centralised laboratory; preprint not peer reviewed.
studies.title: AI-Assisted Tissue-Based Antibody Interpretation in Autoimmune Encephalitis: Prospective Validation and Reader Study

studies.design: Real-world multi-site non-randomised comparison of AI-assisted vs standard clinics
studies.ai_system: Real-time AI decision support for dermoscopic lesion selection
studies.humans: Skin cancer screening nurses (with teledermatologists as reference)
studies.finding: In nurse-led teledermoscopy screening of 1,102,382 lesions, AI-assisted screening had a higher malignancy detection rate than standard screening (25.5 vs 15.7 malignancies per 1,000 lesions; adjusted odds ratio 1.73, 95% CI 1.68-1.77), consistent across nurse-experience tiers.
studies.limitation: Non-randomised allocation and teledermatologist diagnosis as reference standard, so findings are associational; preprint not peer reviewed.
studies.title: AI-assisted nurse-led skin cancer screening in a teledermoscopy framework: a multi-site evaluation with one million lesions

studies.design: Benchtop phantom and in vivo animal study
studies.ai_system: Deep learning IVUS segmentation with CT fusion AR guidance
studies.finding: Endovascular cannulation with AR guidance versus fluoroscopy alone. AR guidance significantly reduced cannulation time, radiation exposure, and cognitive workload; numbers not reported in abstract.
studies.limitation: Preprint; phantom and ovine models only, no numbers or surgeon count given.
studies.title: Learned ultrasound segmentation and deformable CT fusion for augmented reality endovascular surgery

studies.design: Prospective validation with blinded expert qualitative rating of AI vs expert segmentations
studies.humans: Expert segmentations; rated by two interventional neuroradiologists
studies.finding: Cerebral artery segmentation on 3D rotational angiography in 40 patients was rated blind by two interventional neuroradiologists. Global quality scores were significantly lower for nnUNet v2 than for expert segmentations (median 4 vs 5, p<0.001). Segmentations were rated clinically usable in 88-90% of cases for nnUNet v2 versus 95-98% for experts, without significant difference on the binary usability criterion.
studies.limitation: Small prospective test set (40 patients) with only two raters; preprint, not peer reviewed.
studies.title: Automated Segmentation of Cerebral Arteries on Three-Dimensional Rotational Angiography Using nnUNet v2: Prospective Validation with Quantitative Metrics and Expert Qualitative Assessment

studies.design: Single-centre propensity-score-matched comparison of AI CAD-assisted versus conventional colonoscopy
studies.finding: In 786 matched colonoscopies, the adenoma detection rate was 41.5% with AI CAD versus 34.4% without (adjusted OR = 1.380; P = 0.042). The polyp detection rate was 53.2% vs 46.1%, which was not significant (P = 0.077).
studies.limitation: Single-centre non-randomised observational preprint; residual confounding is possible and the number of endoscopists is not stated.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence Significantly Improves Adenoma Detection Rate but Does Not Affect Polyp Detection Rate in Colonoscopy: A Propensity Score Matching Study

studies.design: Retrospective comparison on 404 EHR cases converted to synthetic vignettes
studies.ai_system: CLMBR-T structured EHR model and eight LLMs (e.g., DeepSeek V3, Claude 4.1 Opus, GPT-5)
studies.finding: Physicians, an EHR-trained ML model and LLMs predicted 30-day ED visits and unplanned admissions. CLMBR-T achieved AUROC 0.79 (95% CI: 0.75-0.83) and large LLMs AUROC 0.74, while pooled physicians performed lowest (AUROC 0.65, 95% CI: 0.59-0.70). Individual physician AUROC ranged 0.55-0.83, with three of 35 exceeding the ML benchmark.
studies.limitation: Preprint; physicians and LLMs judged GPT-5-generated synthetic vignettes while the ML model used original structured data.
studies.title: From Clinical Judgement to Large Language Models: Benchmarking Predictive Approaches for Unplanned Hospital Admissions

studies.design: Benchmark of LLMs vs clinicians on script concordance tests
studies.finding: On 750 Script Concordance Test questions, GPT-4o scored highest (63.6% ± 1.2%) among LLMs. Models matched or exceeded student performance on multiple examinations but did not reach the level of senior residents or attending physicians.
studies.limitation: Exam-style questions rather than real care; human scores drawn from existing datasets; preprint.
studies.title: Do Language Models Think Like Doctors?

studies.design: Single-centre cross-sectional study; 50 case notes from real pediatric histories
studies.humans: Volunteer doctors of varying experience at a pediatric hospital
studies.finding: Top-5 differential diagnosis on 50 pediatric cases of common and rare diseases. Top-5 accuracy was 65% for clinicians and 60% for DxGPT, with no significant differences; for rare diseases 50% vs 49%.
studies.limitation: Preprint; single centre, 50 cases, each clinician reviewed only 3 cases.
studies.title: Evaluation of the Clinical Utility of DxGPT, a GPT-4 Based Large Language Model, through an Analysis of Diagnostic Accuracy and User Experience

studies.design: Double-blind, randomized-sequence 2x2 factorial evaluation of LLM antibiotic regimens versus real physician prescriptions on 59 complex inpatient infection cases, rated by three senior clinicians
studies.ai_system: MedGo and DeepSeek V3.5, with and without chain-of-thought prompting
studies.finding: Antibiotic regimens for 59 complex inpatient infection cases were scored 1-5 by three senior clinicians. Real physicians scored 4.76±0.04, ahead of MedGo-CoT (4.58±0.09), DeepSeek-CoT (4.41±0.11), MedGo (4.25±0.16) and DeepSeek (3.98±0.20) (Friedman test, p<0.001).
studies.limitation: Preprint; small case set (59) with only three raters; number of physicians who wrote prescriptions not stated.
studies.title: General-Purpose vs. Domain-Specific Large Language Models in Antibiotic Clinical Decision-Making: A Double-Blind Evaluation with a 2X2 Factorial Design

studies.design: Multisite retrospective validation on 500 sampled inpatient admissions against physician-adjudicated chart review
studies.ai_system: inHealth General Reasoner (iHGR), EHR-integrated generative AI
studies.humans: Clinicians using checklist-based and judgement-based order sets
studies.finding: For inpatient VTE risk stratification, iHGR achieved 81.8% sensitivity (95% CI 77.3-85.6) and 70.9% specificity (63.6-77.3). Clinician checklist-based order sets had 61.3% sensitivity and 86.2% specificity, and clinician judgement-based order sets 78.1% sensitivity and 65.4% specificity.
studies.limitation: Preprint; retrospective in silico evaluation at one health system; trade-off between sensitivity and specificity.
studies.title: Multisite Real-World Validation of an Electronic Health Record-Integrated Generative Artificial Intelligence Tool for Venous Thromboembolism Risk Stratification

studies.design: Retrospective model development and evaluation on expert-adjudicated dataset
studies.ai_system: Image-based ConvNeXt ensemble for ECG classification
studies.finding: On a held-out test set of emergency ECG images across 12 categories, the ConvNeXt ensemble achieved a macro F1-score of 0.807 (95% CI, 0.788-0.825), compared with 0.820 (95% CI, 0.805-0.832) for annotating cardiologists.
studies.limitation: Preprint; single-institution dataset with cardiologists also providing reference labels.
studies.title: Image-based deep learning for emergency electrocardiogram classification

studies.design: Two-phase diagnostic accuracy study against adjudicated reference standard
studies.finding: In 2,256 ED attendances, LLM balanced accuracy matched or outperformed clinician review in identifying alcohol (0.942 v 0.930, p=0.635), drug (0.959 v 0.791, p<0.001) and self-harm (0.982 v 0.908, p=0.004) involvement.
studies.limitation: Preprint; single UK emergency department.
studies.title: Half of alcohol, drug, and self-harm presentations cannot be identified in coded emergency department data: a diagnostic accuracy study of a large language model

studies.design: Retrospective cross-vendor validation on screening mammography cohort
studies.ai_system: Three FDA-cleared commercial mammography AI CAD algorithms and Mirai
studies.finding: On 707,922 screening exams, radiologists recalled 6.8% with a sensitivity of 67.2%. The best algorithm (D, AUROC 0.849) had sensitivity from 55.3% at 5% to 77.9% at 25% AI-positive rate, and no algorithm matched radiologist sensitivity at AI-positive rates of 10% or less.
studies.limitation: Retrospective comparison; radiologist comparison is secondary and depends on chosen operating point; preprint.
studies.title: Kaiser Permanente National Cross-Vendor Validation of Mammography Artificial Intelligence Computer-Aided Diagnosis Algorithms in a US-Representative Population

studies.design: Retrospective decision concordance study
studies.finding: Surgical indication and level for degenerative lumbar spine disease in 147 patients versus senior-surgeon ground truth. LLMs had higher therapy-decision accuracy (66.0%-68.0%) than residents (54.4%) but over-recommended surgery; conditional level accuracy was 71.4% for residents versus 33.3%-41.1% for LLMs.
studies.limitation: Preprint; only two residents, single-centre retrospective.
studies.title: Multimodal Large Language Models vs. Medical Doctors in Degenerative Lumbar Spine Surgery: A Retrospective Decision Concordance Study of 147 Patients

studies.design: Retrospective cohort of ED encounters; physicians vs GPT-5 applying the Fabre framework on a validation subset
studies.ai_system: GPT-5 (and XGBoost model Cultryx vs clinical heuristics)
studies.finding: On a validation subset, physicians and GPT-5 applied the Fabre framework to decide blood culture need for bacteremia. Physicians achieved 95.7% sensitivity versus 71.6% for GPT-5.
studies.limitation: Preprint; retrospective record-based comparison on a subset, number of physicians not stated.
studies.title: Cultryx: Precision Diagnostic Stewardship for Blood Cultures Using Machine Learning

studies.design: Vignette study comparing LLM differential diagnoses with doctors' diagnoses across five countries
studies.ai_system: ChatGPT, Claude Sonnet, Google Gemini, Microsoft Copilot
studies.humans: Doctors from Ghana, India, Jordan, Brazil and the UK
studies.finding: Doctors and LLMs gave top-4 diagnoses for five respiratory vignettes; 106 unique diagnoses were offered by 21 doctors and 53 by LLMs. LLMs proposed 50% (95% CI 32.6 to 67.4%) of doctors' diagnoses in the UK versus 32.0% (95% CI 23.1 to 42.3%) in LMICs (Chi-squared p = 0.028).
studies.limitation: Preprint; only five vignettes and 21 doctors, with doctors' diagnoses used as reference rather than a ground truth.
studies.title: Bias in respiratory diagnoses by Large Language Models (LLMs) in Low Middle Income Countries (LMICs)

studies.design: Reader study using MR CLEAN trial data; neurologists predicted 3-month mRS unaided and assisted by a prognostic model, benchmarked against standalone models
studies.ai_system: MR PREDICTS feature-based model and a multimodal interpretable deep learning model
studies.finding: Six neurologists predicted three-month mRS for 40 LVO stroke patients. For the full mRS distribution, MR PREDICTS (QWK 0.51) and the DL model (QWK 0.49) significantly outperformed unaided neurologists (QWK 0.27), while binary mRS accuracy was comparable (64.17% unaided vs 67.50% and 63.16% for the models). Model assistance modestly improved neurologists' predictions (QWK 0.41; binary accuracy 68.75%).
studies.limitation: Only six neurologists and 40 patients from retrospective trial data; preprint, not peer reviewed.
studies.title: Human Intuition vs. Computational Precision: Neurologists, Feature-based Models, and Deep Learning for Stroke Prognosis

studies.design: Retrospective reanalysis of the SUPPORT2 cohort comparing an ML survival model with attending-physician prognostic estimates and the 1995 SUPPORT model
studies.finding: In 9,105 critically ill adults, mortality prediction at fixed horizons was compared. At 60 days the survival model's AUC was 0.750 versus 0.808 for physicians (on the matched sample) and 0.827 for the 1995 model. The physician advantage was conditional on a physician electing to give an estimate.
studies.limitation: Retrospective data from 1989-1994; physician comparison limited to a matched sample where estimates were given; preprint.
studies.title: Ranking-optimized survival models can underperform fixed-horizon clinical prediction: a SUPPORT2 reanalysis of machine learning, attending-physician judgment, and the original SUPPORT model at 60- and 180-day mortality

studies.design: Blinded comparison of LLM vs specialist responses to real Advice & Guidance queries
studies.humans: Specialist neurologists; rated by two neurologists and two GPs
studies.finding: Responses to 50 adult neurology Advice & Guidance cases were compared between MedGemma and specialist neurologists. Blinded ratings showed no significant differences (outcome: 84% vs 82%, p=0.67; safety: 3.98 vs 4.02; efficacy: 4.06 vs 3.98; feasibility: 4.39 vs 4.20). However, 10% of LLM responses received concerning scores compared to 0% of human responses, and unblinded raters preferred human responses.
studies.limitation: Small single-centre pilot (50 cases) with moderate inter-rater agreement; preprint, not peer reviewed.
studies.title: Large Language Model Performance in UK Advice & Guidance: A Pilot Study in Neurology

studies.design: Comparative analysis within a high-fidelity simulation RCT (Anticipamax); diagnostic lotteries ranked with Condorcet method
studies.finding: Residents and ChatGPT-4 produced ranked diagnostic hypotheses for a simulated multifactorial perioperative shock before and after the simulation. The AI identified septic shock among its top hypotheses but missed gas embolism, which residents unanimously identified; both converged on septic shock after clinical evolution. The residents' focused, adaptive reasoning was consistently ranked strategically superior to the AI's exhaustive approach.
studies.limitation: Single simulated scenario with one LLM and a novel, qualitative-leaning ranking framework; preprint, not peer reviewed.
studies.title: The Cognitive Safety Net: Comparing Human and AI Diagnostic Reasoning during Complex Clinical Situations.

studies.design: Retrospective comparison on 131 frozen liver biopsy specimens against permanent-section ground truth
studies.finding: Classification of macrovesicular steatosis in frozen donor liver sections. For binary classification, Prov-GigaPath achieved 96.4% accuracy, UNI 85.7%, and surgical pathologists 84.0% (P = .22); in five-category classification, Prov-GigaPath 57.1%, UNI 50.0%, pathologists 58.7% (P = .70).
studies.limitation: Small single-cohort retrospective sample (68 donors); preprint.
studies.title: Accuracy of Foundation AI Models for Hepatic Macrovesicular Steatosis Quantification in Frozen Sections

studies.design: Retrospective diagnostic study at a German heart centre comparing LLM pipelines, standalone LLMs and treating clinicians against expert-adjudicated risk scores
studies.ai_system: LLM extraction + deterministic computation pipelines (DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3, GPT-4 Turbo, Llama 3.1, PaLM 2)
studies.finding: The task was computing HAS-BLED, CHA2DS2-VASc and EuroSCORE II from clinical reports for 255 patients. Mean Krippendorff's alpha against expert adjudication was 0.79 for pipelines, 0.32 for standalone LLMs and 0.31 for treating clinicians. The Qwen3 pipeline had lower RMSEs than clinicians for HAS-BLED (0.20 vs 0.87), CHA2DS2-VASc (0.53 vs 1.08) and EuroSCORE II (1.99 vs 2.05).
studies.limitation: Single-centre retrospective preprint; the number of clinicians is not stated, and clinician scores come from routine documentation.
studies.title: Development of an LLM Pipeline Surpassing Physicians in Cardiovascular Risk Score Calculation

studies.design: Retrospective ML development with external testing, compared against trained SLPs listening to phonations
studies.ai_system: Machine learning model on voice acoustic features
studies.finding: The task was classifying high versus low aspiration risk from vowel phonations. The model achieved an AUC of 0.70 (0.52-0.88) in external testing. It had better accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, negative and positive predictive values than trained SLPs.
studies.limitation: Small retrospective preprint; SLP numbers and metrics are not reported, and SLPs listened only to phonations rather than performing a usual bedside assessment.
studies.title: Development & Validation of a Machine Learning Model That Uses Voice to Predict Aspiration Risk

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter diagnostic study of 537 cataract surgery video clips comparing general-purpose AI, automated task-specific models and human graders
studies.ai_system: General-purpose AI systems and task-specific models from an automated AI model generator
studies.humans: Human graders of varying experience (junior and senior specialists)
studies.finding: Detecting anterior capsular radial folds in capsulorhexis video, measured by F1 score. The best general-purpose AI achieved a mean F1 of 0.519 and fine-tuned models remained inferior to human graders (maximum F1 score, 0.606). The top automated task-specific model (F1 0.835) matched junior specialists (mean F1 0.829) but remained below senior specialists.
studies.limitation: Preprint, retrospective video-clip study; number of human graders not stated.
studies.title: Automated Task-Specific vs General-Purpose Artificial Intelligence for Detecting Subtle Intraoperative Warning Signs During Cataract Surgery: A Multicenter Diagnostic Study

studies.design: Survey with blinded ranking of responses
studies.humans: Verified physician responses from r/AskDocs; 52 physician raters
studies.finding: Physicians ranked anonymized answers to patient questions from ChatGPT-4.0, Meta.AI and a verified physician. Across all regions, ChatGPT-4.0 and Meta.AI responses were preferred over physician-authored responses, and AI responses consistently outperformed physician responses across years in practice.
studies.limitation: Preprint; small preliminary survey not powered for significance; abstract gives no rank values.
studies.title: Physician Evaluations of Large Language Model-Generated Responses to Medical Questions by Region and Years in Practice: A preliminary study

studies.design: Retrospective comparison across 500 consecutive urgent-care telehealth encounters
studies.finding: The AI system and clinicians were compared on diagnosis and treatment plans in 500 telehealth encounters. Top diagnosis matched in 81% of cases and treatment plans aligned in 99.2%; in expert review of discordant cases, AI was superior in 36.1% and humans in 9.3%.
studies.limitation: Preprint; retrospective concordance analysis partly adjudicated by an LLM, without patient outcomes.
studies.title: Toward the Autonomous AI Doctor: Quantitative Benchmarking of an Autonomous Agentic AI Versus Board-Certified Clinicians in a Real World Setting

studies.design: Retrospective comparison against pathology in 50 CNS tumor patients
studies.finding: ChatGPT and a neuroradiologist generated differential diagnoses of CNS tumors from MRI characteristics, with pathology as reference. ChatGPT's overall accuracy was 48% versus 70% for the neuroradiologist; agreement with pathology was kappa = 0.419.
studies.limitation: Preprint; single centre, 50 patients and a single neuroradiologist comparator.
studies.title: The Potential of ChatGPT as an Aiding Tool for the Neuroradiologist

studies.design: Mixed-methods study comparing AI triage urgency with GP ratings for same-day appointment requests
studies.finding: AI urgency scores were compared with GP-assigned ratings for 649 same-day appointment requests. Correlation was strong (rho=0.796) with 83.7% categorical agreement across eight urgency levels (kappa 0.69); the AI tended to over-triage and rarely under-triaged.
studies.limitation: Preprint; agreement with GP ratings rather than an independent outcome reference standard, single setting.
studies.title: Benchmarking Artificial Intelligence vs General Practitioners Decision-Making in Same-Day Appointments Triage: A Mixed-Methods Study in UK Primary Care

studies.design: Retrospective cohort comparing AI human-in-the-loop screening with standard of care
studies.humans: Generalist physicians triaging AI-flagged cases vs standard-of-care clinicians
studies.finding: Across 899,862 EHRs, AI-based human-in-the-loop screening triaged 191 cases and standard of care 107 for acute hepatic porphyria. Clinically plausible cases were 74 (38.74%) for HAI and 28 (27.72%) for SOC, with 46 de-novo cases missed by SOC.
studies.limitation: Preprint; retrospective single-centre, industry-funded, plausibility judged by specialists rather than confirmed diagnosis.
studies.title: Unmet Needs in Acute Hepatic Porphyria Diagnosis: A Comparative Big Data Analysis of an AI-based Human-in-the-Loop Screening Versus Standard of Care

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of ML models, LLMs and physicians predicting outcomes from discharge summaries
studies.ai_system: Trained machine learning models and commercial LLMs
studies.finding: ML models, LLMs and physicians predicted 30-day mortality and readmission from MIMIC-IV discharge summaries. Machine learning models demonstrated superior performance compared to both LLMs and human evaluators, though none achieved a Matthews Correlation Coefficient > 0.8.
studies.limitation: Retrospective use of discharge summaries only; number of physicians not stated; preprint.
studies.title: Predicting 30-Day Mortality and Readmission Using Hospital Discharge Summaries: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models, Large Language Models and Physicians

studies.design: Retrospective crossover reader study with 3-week washout
studies.finding: 20 pathologists scored 200 breast cancer HER2 IHC cases with and without AIM-HER2. AI assistance improved inter-rater agreement overall and at the 0/1+ and 1+/2+ cutoffs, and significantly increased PPA at those cutoffs.
studies.limitation: Retrospective reader study; accuracy depended on reference panel composition; preprint.
studies.title: Impact of a machine learning-powered algorithm on pathologist HER2 IHC scoring in breast cancer

studies.design: Retrospective comparison on real neurology cases
studies.finding: On 28 anonymized neurology patient records assessed against discharge diagnoses, neurologists achieved a diagnostic accuracy of 75%, versus ChatGPT-3.5 (54%) and Gemini (46%). Both LLMs over-prescribed diagnostic tests in 17-25% of cases.
studies.limitation: Only 28 cases from a single centre; number of neurologists not stated; preprint.
studies.title: Is it time for the neurologist to use Large Language Models in everyday practice?

studies.design: Comparative diagnostic accuracy study of AI screening tool vs first-year residents against expert annotations, plus combined approach
studies.finding: In 435 adult patients, AI outperformed residents for glaucoma suspect classification accuracy (88.6% vs 82.9%, p = 0.016) and had lower CDR mean absolute error (0.056 vs 0.105). For retinal disease, AI had higher sensitivity (90.1% vs 63.0% for medium/high-risk) and specificity (95.8% vs 90.4%); the combined AI+resident approach reached the highest sensitivity (80.4% for glaucoma suspect; 92.6% for medium/high-risk retinal disease).
studies.limitation: Preprint, single tertiary centre, comparison only with first-year residents; number of residents not stated.
studies.title: Comparative Performance of an AI Tool and First-Year Residents in Retinal Disease and Glaucoma Assessments: A Study in a Mexican Tertiary Care Setting

studies.design: Retrospective multi-institutional diagnostic accuracy study comparing DL models and RSIrs-max with expert PI-RADS
studies.finding: For patient-level csPCa detection in 1,892 patients, RSIrs-max and the DL model (AUC 0.75 and 0.78) performed comparably to expert PI-RADS (AUC 0.73). Combining the DL model with PI-RADS gave AUC 0.81 (P<.001) versus 0.73 for PI-RADS alone.
studies.limitation: Preprint; retrospective with PI-RADS from clinical reads, not a reader study of radiologists using AI; reader number not stated.
studies.title: Deep learning AI and Restriction Spectrum Imaging for patient-level detection of clinically significant prostate cancer on MRI

studies.design: Retrospective model development study with comparison to junior radiologists
studies.ai_system: Fine-tuned pre-trained and large language models on radiology report findings
studies.finding: Across four brain disease classification tasks, the best language model reached an average AUC of 84.75% and accuracy of 79.48%. It outperformed junior radiologists by 9.47% in accuracy.
studies.limitation: Preprint; human comparison is secondary and reported only as a difference, with reader number not stated.
studies.title: Simple Words over Rich Imaging: Accurate Brain Disease Classification via Language Model Analysis of Radiological Reports

studies.design: Retrospective model development with comparison to actual clinician prescribing
studies.finding: In Enterobacterales bloodstream infections treated with a beta-lactam, clinician prescribing led to 70% receiving an active beta-lactam (30% under-treated). Model predictions without species data could have led to 79% receiving an active beta-lactam (21% under-treated).
studies.limitation: Preprint; retrospective counterfactual comparison at a single region, not prospective use.
studies.title: Machine learning to predict antibiotic susceptibility in Enterobacterales bloodstream infections compared to clinician prescribing

studies.design: Retrospective multicenter cohort; fine-tuned model tested on 150 pediatric encounters compared with physicians
studies.finding: Pediatric differential diagnosis on 150 rural encounters. The fine-tuned GPT-3 model achieved accuracy of 87% (131/150) versus 91% for human physicians (P = .47).
studies.limitation: Preprint; small test set from one rural organization; number and role of comparison physicians not described.
studies.title: Evaluating the accuracy and reliability of large language models in assisting with pediatric differential diagnoses: A multicenter diagnostic study

studies.design: Retrospective comparison on 99 consecutive real brain MRI reports with pathology ground truth
studies.finding: ChatGPT and five radiologists suggested differential and final diagnoses from brain tumor MRI report findings. ChatGPT achieved a final diagnostic accuracy of 75% (95% CI: 66, 83%) versus radiologists' 64% to 82%; for differential diagnoses ChatGPT reached 95% (95% CI: 91, 99%) versus 74% to 88% for radiologists.
studies.limitation: Single-centre preprint with only five radiologists, using text reports rather than images.
studies.title: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT's Diagnostic Performance with Radiologists Using Real-World Radiology Reports of Brain Tumors

studies.design: Retrospective evaluation on 10,000 randomly selected ED visit notes
studies.finding: GPT-3.5-turbo made recommendations on admission, radiological investigation and antibiotic prescription from ED clinical notes. It performed poorly compared with a resident physician, with accuracy scores 24% lower on average, and was overly cautious (high sensitivity at the cost of specificity).
studies.limitation: Preprint; comparison against a single resident physician reference, older model, zero-shot only.
studies.title: Evaluating the use of GPT-3.5-turbo to provide clinical recommendations in the Emergency Department

studies.design: Multi-reviewer evaluation of ChatGPT versus physician responses to diabetes patients' questions
studies.finding: In a real-world dataset, responses from ChatGPT and physicians to questions from three people with type 2 diabetes were rated. ChatGPT received lower ratings than physicians (helpfulness: 4.18 vs. 4.91, P <0.001; trustworthiness: 4.80 vs. 5.20, P = 0.042), but with carefully crafted prompts ratings were comparable.
studies.limitation: Preprint; only three patients' questions in the comparison and number of responding physicians not stated.
studies.title: Exploration of ChatGPT application in diabetes education: a multi-dataset, multi-reviewer study

studies.design: Retrospective single-centre comparison of a deep learning EMG classifier with six physicians on 58 subjects
studies.ai_system: One-dimensional convolutional neural network with divide-and-vote system for needle EMG
studies.humans: Six physicians experienced in performing and interpreting electromyography
studies.finding: Classifying myopathy, neuropathy or normal from needle EMG, the model had accuracy 0.875, sensitivity 0.820, specificity 0.904 and PPV 0.820, versus 0.694, 0.537, 0.773 and 0.524 for physicians. The model's AUCs were better than the averaged results of the six physicians.
studies.limitation: Preprint, not peer reviewed; small single-centre sample of 58 subjects and only six physicians.
studies.title: Deep learning-based algorithm versus physician judgement for diagnosis of myopathy and neuropathy from needle electromyography

studies.design: Retrospective evaluation on pairs of real ED visits
studies.finding: Identifying the higher-acuity patient from pairs of ED physician note histories. On a 500-pair subsample, GPT-3.5 achieved accuracy 0.84 and F1 0.85 versus the resident physician's accuracy 0.86 and F1 0.87.
studies.limitation: Single resident physician comparator on a subsample; preprint not peer reviewed.
studies.title: Assessing clinical acuity in the Emergency Department using the GPT-3.5 Artificial Intelligence Model

studies.design: Blinded physician rating of AI vs manual contours on retrospective CT test sets
studies.humans: Radiation oncologists and a resident physician (manual contours)
studies.finding: Contouring head and neck lymph node levels for radiotherapy planning. Across all physician-generated contours 82% were rated usable with stylistic to no edits versus 92% of AI-generated contours; preference differed significantly only for RP contours (p < 0.01).
studies.limitation: Single-centre retrospective data with small test sets; preprint not peer reviewed.
studies.title: Clinical Acceptability of Automatically Generated Lymph Node Levels and Structures of Deglutition and Mastication for Head and Neck Cancer Patient Radiation Treatment Planning

studies.design: Retrospective comparison of ChatGPT with four prompting strategies against ophthalmologists and interns on 1226 Chinese fundus fluorescein angiography reports
studies.finding: ChatGPT diagnosed retinal vascular diseases from 1226 Chinese FFA reports. With English prompt for direct diagnosis it achieved F1-score of 80.05%, inferior to ophthalmologists (89.35%) but close to ophthalmologist interns (82.69%). Misinformation (1.96%) and hallucination (0.59%) were observed.
studies.limitation: Preprint, not peer reviewed; text reports rather than images; number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: Transforming Retinal Vascular Disease Classification: A Comprehensive Analysis of ChatGPT's Performance and Inference Abilities on Non-English Clinical Environment

studies.design: Single-centre retrospective observational study of an AI algorithm for 10 chest CT pathologies, validated by experts, versus radiologists' reports without AI
studies.ai_system: Complex AI algorithm for 10 chest CT pathologies
studies.humans: Radiologists reporting without AI; two expert validators
studies.finding: On 160 chest CTs, AI identified 90 studies (56%) with pathologies, of which 81 studies (51%) had at least one pathology missing from the radiologist report. Lost potential revenue for pathologies missed by radiologists but detected by AI was RUB 2,065,360, and AI use was estimated to bring 3.6 times more benefits than the standard model.
studies.limitation: Preprint; single-centre retrospective study with small sample, and outcome framed partly economically; AI findings verified by only two experts.
studies.title: A diagnostic and economic evaluation of the complex artificial intelligence algorithm aimed to detect 10 pathologies on the chest CT images

studies.design: Development and agreement study comparing AI %TBSA estimates with three clinicians on 16 photographs
studies.ai_system: BurnCare two-stage deep learning platform (ResNet50-U-Net, DenseNet169-U-Net)
studies.finding: BurnCare estimated %TBSA from smartphone burn photographs. Its automatic estimate correlated with the mean of three clinicians' estimates (r = 0.746, MAE = 6.29, RMSE = 8.63 percentage points; n = 16), improving to r = 0.853 after manual mask correction; ICC among the three clinicians alone was 0.728.
studies.limitation: Only 16 photographs and three clinicians, with clinicians as the reference rather than an independent ground truth; preprint.
studies.title: BurnCare: A deep learning framework for burn injury assessment and TBSA estimation.

studies.design: Retrospective single-centre study of multimodal LLMs versus radiologists on MRI slices
studies.ai_system: GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 5, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Qwen 3.6
studies.finding: Differentiating glioma from brain abscess on 60 MRI examinations, model accuracy was 0.52-0.73 versus 0.78 and 0.73 for radiologists. Referral text drove model decisions (text-driven span 0.79-1.00).
studies.limitation: Single slice per case, 60 cases, only two radiologists, descriptive comparison; preprint.
studies.title: Clinical referral text overrides MRI evidence in multimodal large language models: glioma versus brain abscess

studies.design: Preregistered benchmark; 49 LLMs and 8 clinicians classified 400 statements for suicidal ideation inserted at varying conversational depth in psychotherapy and synthetic transcripts
studies.finding: LLMs and clinicians performed binary classification of suicidal ideation in statements inserted at 0-200 turns of transcripts. LLM F1 declined with depth across model families (p<0.001), while clinicians showed no decline (mean F1 0.86 at both 0 and 200 turns); eight of nine proprietary models exceeded clinician performance at 200 turns.
studies.limitation: Preprint; only 8 clinicians; statements inserted into transcripts rather than live clinical assessment.
studies.title: Conversational trajectory degrades large language model detection of suicidal ideation relative to clinicians: a preregistered study

studies.design: Standalone verification of an AI histology scoring tool against pathologists using consensus agreement metrics
studies.finding: For ulcerative colitis biopsy histology scoring, AIM-HI UC was non-inferior to pathologists (N=3) for all seven Geboes subgrades, grade-level Geboes, RHI, NHI and histologic improvement/remission endpoints. It was superior for several Geboes subgrades (GS 0, GS 1, GS 2B, GS 5), grade-level Geboes, RHI, and positive percent agreement of 2A histologic remission.
studies.limitation: Preprint; only three comparator pathologists; agreement measured against consensus rather than clinical outcomes.
studies.title: Standardized, repeatable ulcerative colitis histology scoring and endpoint assessment using an automated, foundation model-based tool

studies.design: Retrospective development and test of segmentation models compared with human readers using FROC analysis
studies.finding: For detection of perfusion defects on planar V/Q scans in a hold-out set of 46 high-probability patients, BTU-Net was the only model performing on par with human readers on FROC analysis. At 1.5 false positives per projection, BTU-Net sensitivity was 0.529 ± 0.026.
studies.limitation: Preprint; single-centre retrospective; small test set; human reader numbers and results not quantified in abstract.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Detection of Vascular Perfusion Defects on Ventilation/Perfusion (V/Q) Scintigraphy for Pulmonary Embolism

studies.design: Retrospective paired crossover reader study
studies.ai_system: nnU-Net deep learning vascular segmentation for CTA
studies.finding: Ten readers assessed vertebral artery dissection on 40 external CTAs with and without segmentation-based augmentation. Diagnostic accuracy was lower with augmentation than without (0.72 vs 0.84, P < 0.001), while confidence (3.98 vs 3.96) and interpretation time (137.3 vs 166.7 seconds) did not differ significantly.
studies.limitation: Preprint; small external test set (40 CTAs) and only 10 readers.
studies.title: Does Deep Learning Vascular Segmentation on CTA Improve Vertebral Artery Dissection Detection?

studies.design: Standardized-patient methodology study with blinded clinician rating of transcripts; exploratory resident vs chatbot comparison
studies.finding: In standardized-patient primary care intake encounters (32 resident-led, 69 chatbot-led) rated by blinded clinicians, residents asked about more critical elements (adjusted difference 12.5 percentage points; 95% CI, 7.0 to 18.1) and satisfactorily addressed more (9.2 points; 3.8 to 14.6). Totals did not differ.
studies.limitation: Exploratory comparison in a small simulated pilot with poor inter-rater agreement for totals; preprint not peer reviewed.
studies.title: A Methodology to Evaluate the Efficacy and Patient-Centeredness of a Patient-Facing AI Chatbot: Development and Validation of a Standardized-Patient Method

studies.design: Retrospective model development with radiologist comparison
studies.finding: Classification of vertebral metastatic lesion quality on CT. The 3D model achieved ensemble accuracy of 84.7% with Cohen's kappa = 0.76 against the radiologist and comparable sensitivity and specificity across lesion subtypes; both struggled with osteolytic lesions.
studies.limitation: Preprint; single radiologist comparator, single-centre retrospective data.
studies.title: Deep Learning-Based Classification of Bone Lesions on CT Scans of Metastatic Spine Disease Patients: A 3D-Convolutional Neural Network Approach

studies.design: Model development with blinded reader study
studies.ai_system: HATS (pathology foundation model with attention MIL)
studies.finding: Predicting lymphoma subtype from H&E morphology alone. In a blinded reader study HATS outperformed practicing pathologists (85% vs 65%).
studies.limitation: Preprint; reader number not stated and pathologists restricted to morphology without IHC.
studies.title: Harnessing Pathology Foundation Models to Accelerate Lymphoma Diagnosis Through Automated Immunohistochemistry Triage

studies.design: Model development with reader study
studies.finding: Breast cancer detection on mammography. In a reader study (n>1,200) the model outperformed radiologists by an absolute AUC margin of 24% on extended follow-up.
studies.limitation: Preprint; reader study details and radiologist numbers not given in abstract.
studies.title: Towards Accessible Radiological Image Analysis via Local Agentic Framework: Validation in Mammography

studies.design: Retrospective multicohort model development with dermatologist comparison
studies.ai_system: Multi-endpoint non-invasive AI framework for BCC
studies.finding: Triage, subtyping and depth assessment of suspected basal cell carcinoma. Performance exceeded the 19-dermatologist mean on matched cases for every prespecified primary metric (all P ≤ 0.014).
studies.limitation: Preprint; retrospective, with out-of-scope routing errors noted.
studies.title: Endpoint-aligned artificial intelligence for biopsy-sparing assessment of suspected basal cell carcinoma

studies.design: Retrospective multicentre study with blinded reader study
studies.ai_system: MIMIC weakly supervised deep learning model
studies.finding: Distinguishing early mycosis fungoides from benign inflammatory dermatoses on 171 H&E slides, morphology only. MIMIC achieved AUROC 0.87, exceeding the mean pathologist AUROC (0.79) and the best individual reader (0.83).
studies.limitation: Preprint; retrospective European cohorts, morphology-only reading.
studies.title: Histological triage of early-stage mycosis fungoides using a weakly supervised deep learning-based model: a multicentre, external validation, and clinical utility study

studies.design: Blinded comparative study of responses to 49 Reddit r/AskDocs otology questions, scored by five evaluators
studies.finding: Answering patient otologic questions, LLM responses were rated higher than physician responses in quality (10.95 vs 9.58), empathy (7.26 vs 5.18) and readability (4.00 vs 3.73), all p < .05. LLM responses were also longer (mean 145 vs 67 words). Evaluators identified AI versus physician responses correctly in 89.4% of cases.
studies.limitation: Preprint. Physician answers came from an online forum rather than clinical care, and blinding was weak since evaluators identified the source in 89.4% of cases.
studies.title: A Blinded Comparative Evaluation of Clinical and AI-Generated Responses to Otologic Patient Queries

studies.design: Cross-sectional validation on 41 test images, with AI agreement compared against blinded dermatologists and non-specialist physicians
studies.ai_system: Two-stage EfficientNet B7 CNN pipeline for atopic dermatitis severity grading
studies.humans: Two blinded dermatologists and two blinded non-specialist physicians
studies.finding: Grading erythema severity in atopic dermatitis photographs. AI agreement with dermatologist consensus was substantial (accuracy 80.7%; kappa = 0.68), while agreement with physician consensus was lower (accuracy 54.8%; kappa = 0.34). For excoriation and lichenification, AI-dermatologist agreement was moderate (accuracy 72.4%, kappa 0.62; accuracy 71.4%, kappa 0.59).
studies.limitation: Preprint with a small validation set (41 images). One rater took part in both training annotation and validation scoring.
studies.title: Grading of Erythema and Visual Attributes in Atopic Dermatitis across Diverse Skin Tones Using a Vision AI Pipeline

studies.design: Retrospective model development with small-lesion reader study (n = 200 CTs)
studies.finding: In a reader study of 200 CT scans for small pancreatic lesion detection, SCOPE achieved a lesion-versus-normal AUC of 0.922 and performed within the range of subspecialty abdominal radiologists. SCOPE provided the correct diagnosis in 14.5% (29/200) of cases in which two or more readers were incorrect.
studies.limitation: Preprint; retrospective enriched reader set, reader numbers and reader metrics not reported.
studies.title: SCOPE: AI-Assisted Early Detection of Potentially Curable Pancreatic Neoplasms on CT from Local and Global Information

studies.design: Retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, 200 POCUS cases from four hospitals
studies.finding: The device's cardiac POCUS measurements were compared with the average of three cardiologists, with inter-cardiologist RMSE as reference. RMSE for LV ejection fraction was 6.20% vs inter-cardiologist 8.23%, and for IVC maximal diameter 0.25cm vs 0.36cm; the device met passing criteria for six of seven measurements, though LV end diastolic diameter RMSE was 5.06mm vs 4.67mm.
studies.limitation: Retrospective, reference standard is the cardiologists' own average with only three readers; preprint.
studies.title: Cardiac Measurement Calculation on Point-of-Care Ultrasonography with Artificial Intelligence

studies.design: Benchmark of an LLM diagnostic agent on 302 NEJM CPC cases compared with AMIE and physicians
studies.ai_system: OpenMedicine AI (LLM agent with deterministic controller)
studies.finding: On 302 NEJM CPC cases, OpenMedicine AI achieved 46.0% Top-1 and 79.1% Top-10 differential-diagnosis accuracy, compared with 15.6% and 20.9% for physicians. It rescued 99 of 302 cases missed by physicians (OR 16.5).
studies.limitation: Preprint using published CPC cases with physician data apparently drawn from prior work; the number of physicians is not stated and the cases may not reflect real practice.
studies.title: Toward Accurate and Actionable Differential Diagnosis with Lean LLM Orchestration

studies.design: Multimodal AI development and validation with a clinical usability study of physicians with and without explainable AI
studies.finding: Predicting immunotherapy outcomes in NSCLC. In the clinical usability study, expert and non-expert physicians could improve their prediction with the explainable AI tool; no physician-level numbers are reported in the abstract.
studies.limitation: Preprint; usability study details, sample size and effect sizes not reported in abstract.
studies.title: I3LUNG: Clinical Validation of a Multimodal AI Tool to Support Immunotherapy Decisions in NSCLC

studies.design: Multi-reader retrospective study on thermal images of 258 symptomatic participants
studies.finding: Breast cancer detection on thermal images. Thermalytix had sensitivity 95.2% and specificity 66.7%; readers had sensitivity/specificity of 60.3%/81.5%, 74.6%/50.8% and 71.4%/63.8%. AUROC of Thermalytix was 0.85, 13.7% greater than manual interpretation.
studies.limitation: Preprint with only three readers and retrospective data from a prior trial; vendor-associated evaluation possible.
studies.title: Radiomic Analysis of Breast Thermal Images Using Thermalytix: A Multi-case, Multit-reader Study Against Manual Interpretation

studies.design: Patient acceptability study during a divisional clinical examination
studies.finding: AI-DOCS conducted complex patient assessments during a clinical examination and was compared with basic physician trainees on acceptability. It scored similarly to trainees on empathy, politeness and comprehensiveness, and elicited clinical information not divulged to human examiners.
studies.limitation: Preprint; abstract reports no numbers or sample sizes and the setting is an examination.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence Deployment of Conversational Support (AI-DOCS): A patient acceptability study

studies.design: Retrospective comparison on two multi-institutional histopathology datasets
studies.finding: AI and pathologists estimated tumor-stroma ratio on histopathology. On TCGA-BRCA the AI achieved ICC 0.69 with human consensus, scoring on average 5 percentage points higher, and was more consistent (discrepancy ratio 0.86). On an external dataset (n=357) AI scores were 7 percentage points lower with ICC 0.59.
studies.limitation: Preprint; number of pathologists not stated and no ground truth beyond human scores.
studies.title: A quantitative comparison between human experts and AI at estimating tumor-stroma ratio

studies.design: Benchmarking study with expert-rated responses
studies.ai_system: Gemini-2, GPT-4o, o3 mini, Deepseek R1, Meditron-70B
studies.finding: LLMs and local clinicians answered clinical questions from community health workers, with 524 pairs rated on 11 metrics. Gemini-2 and GPT-4o scored mean 4.49 and 4.48 out of 5, and all LLMs significantly outperformed local clinicians (ps < 0.001), with Gemini-2 surpassing local GPs by an average 0.83 points.
studies.limitation: Preprint; rubric-based rating of written answers rather than patient outcomes; number of clinicians not stated.
studies.title: How Good Are Large Language Models at Supporting Frontline Healthcare Workers in Low-Resource Settings: A Benchmarking Study & Dataset

studies.design: Simulated interactive diagnostic platform study
studies.ai_system: Gregory multi-agent system and base LLMs
studies.finding: On 16 simulated neurological cases, human neurologists achieved 81% diagnostic accuracy (79% residents, 88% specialists), base LLMs 81-94%, and Gregory perfect accuracy. Gregory's diagnostic costs averaged $1,423 vs $3,041 for neurologists (p=0.008), and time to diagnosis was 23 vs 43 days (p=0.002).
studies.limitation: Preprint; small sample of 14 neurologists and 16 simulated cases.
studies.title: AI vs Human Performance in Conversational Hospital-Based Neurological Diagnosis

studies.design: Retrospective single-center model development with comparison to radiologist
studies.ai_system: ResNeXt-based DCNN with double transfer learning
studies.finding: The model classified mammographic microcalcifications against histopathology and was compared with a radiologist's BI-RADS assessment. The DCNN achieved AUC 0.76 with 65% sensitivity and 83% specificity, while the radiologist achieved AUC 0.65 with 100% sensitivity and 30% specificity.
studies.limitation: Preprint; small single-center dataset and a single radiologist assessment.
studies.title: Improving discriminative ability in mammographic microcalcification classification using deep learning: a novel double transfer learning approach validated with an explainable artificial intelligence technique

studies.design: Comparison of automated HER2 DISH quantification with pathologist assessment
studies.ai_system: Deep learning auto-quantification system for HER2 DISH
studies.finding: HER2 dual in situ hybridization images were assessed by an automated deep learning system and by pathologists. Overall percentage agreement by case was 88. 9% (80/90), with processing time of approximately 1 minute per image versus 10-20 times longer for manual assessment.
studies.limitation: Preprint; agreement-only comparison on 90 cases with no independent reference standard or pathologist numbers reported.
studies.title: Light weight deep learning-based auto-quantification system for bright-filed HER2 dual in situ hybridization image analysis

studies.design: Standalone validation plus simulated diagnostic workflow reader study
studies.finding: Four histopathologists assessed 105 lymph node whole slide images with and without LYDIA for metastasis detection. AI assistance increased pathologists' sensitivity from 77.3% to 87.3% and reduced time-to-diagnosis, with up to 1.59-fold acceleration for micro-metastases (saving 26.5 seconds per WSI).
studies.limitation: Preprint; only four pathologists and 105 slides in a simulated workflow evaluating a commercial tool.
studies.title: Evaluating the performance of LYDIA: an AI-powered decision support system in detection of metastatic tumors in lymph nodes

studies.design: Blinded patient-rated survey comparing AI vs clinician answers to genetic counseling questions
studies.finding: Participants rated AI and clinician answers to questions about Alzheimer's disease and genetics on relevance, trustworthiness and coherence. Participants generally preferred AI responses over human-written ones and rated them higher on all evaluation axes.
studies.limitation: Small sample of 26 raters judging written answers; preprint, not peer reviewed.
studies.title: Patient-centered Evaluation of AI Answers to Genetic Counseling Questions

studies.design: Multicenter retrospective development/validation with observer-performance study, with and without CNN, 4-week interval
studies.ai_system: CNN for hyperdense-artery sign detection on non-contrast CT
studies.humans: Five board-certified and five non-board-certified neurosurgeons
studies.finding: For detecting the hyperdense-artery sign, the CNN had sensitivity 0.79 and specificity 0.87 versus 0.61 and 0.60 for board-certified and 0.61 and 0.66 for non-board-certified neurosurgeons. With the CNN, mean AUC rose from 0.72 to 0.81 (p<0.001) and figure of merit from 0.71 to 0.77 (p=0.005).
studies.limitation: Preprint; retrospective reader study with small validation set (n=129) and 10 readers.
studies.title: Development and Validation of Automated Software for the Detection of Large Vessel Occlusion on Noncontrast CT

studies.design: Vignette study of multimodal LLMs vs physicians with and without images
studies.finding: On 120 vignettes, text-only accuracy was 70.8% for GPT-4o, 59.5% for Claude Sonnet 3.5 and 39.5% for physicians. With images, accuracy was 84.5%, 67.3% and 78.8% respectively, with physicians showing the largest gain.
studies.limitation: Preprint; only three physicians and vignettes from public sources.
studies.title: Visual-Textual Integration in LLMs for Medical Diagnosis: A Quantitative Analysis

studies.design: Clinical vignette simulation study
studies.humans: Physicians from a prior study using the same vignettes
studies.finding: On 328 vignettes, Ubie achieved Top-5 hit accuracy of 63.4% and Top-10 of 71.6%. It compared favorably to the median physician hit accuracy.
studies.limitation: Preprint; physician comparison uses historical data and physician numbers are not reported.
studies.title: Ubie Symptom Checker: A Clinical Vignette Simulation Study

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison using textual descriptions of radiological findings for 60 diseases
studies.finding: Diagnosing complex multisystemic cancer-predisposition syndromes from text descriptions of imaging findings. GPT-4 achieved 63% accuracy versus residents' 22% to 43%; overall average accuracy was 49.3% for AI models versus 29.0% for residents.
studies.limitation: Preprint; only three residents and text descriptions rather than images.
studies.title: Evaluating the Diagnostic Performance of Large Language Models in Identifying Complex Multisystemic Syndromes: A Comparative Study with Radiology Residents

studies.design: Multicenter pivotal clinical trial with reader assessment study
studies.humans: Four residents involved in stroke care
studies.finding: Detection of large vessel occlusion on CT angiography in 595 ischemic stroke patients. The software alone had sensitivity of 86% and specificity of 97%; reading with software assistance improved residents' sensitivity by 4.0% and AUROC by 2.4% (all p < 0.001) compared to readings without AI assistance.
studies.limitation: Preprint, not peer reviewed; only four early-career readers.
studies.title: Automated detection of large vessel occlusion using deep learning: a pivotal multicenter clinical trial and reader assessment study

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on 124 published thoracic radiology cases
studies.finding: Diagnosis of 124 text-based Society of Thoracic Radiology cases. ChatGPT had the highest diagnostic accuracy (53.2%) versus radiologists (52.4% and 41.1%), Bard (33.1%) and Bing (29.8%). In specific cases Radiologist I (65.6%) surpassed ChatGPT (63.5%).
studies.limitation: Preprint; only two radiologists; text-based published cases rather than images or real practice.
studies.title: A Comparative Study: Diagnostic Performance of ChatGPT 3.5, Google Bard, Microsoft Bing, and Radiologists in Thoracic Radiology Cases

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on 106 published musculoskeletal radiology cases
studies.ai_system: GPT-4 based ChatGPT and GPT-4V based ChatGPT
studies.humans: A radiology resident and a board-certified radiologist
studies.finding: Diagnosis of 106 Skeletal Radiology 'Test Yourself' cases. GPT-4 based ChatGPT had accuracy of 43% (46/106) and GPT-4V 8% (9/106), versus 41% (43/106) for the resident and 53% (56/106) for the board-certified radiologist. GPT-4 differences from radiologists were not significant (p = 0.78 and 0.22), while GPT-4V was significantly lower (p < 0.001).
studies.limitation: Preprint; only two readers; published teaching cases.
studies.title: Comparison of the diagnostic accuracy among GPT-4 based ChatGPT, GPT-4V based ChatGPT, and radiologists in musculoskeletal radiology

studies.design: Reader study, pathologists reviewing slides with and without AI assistance
studies.ai_system: AI classifier of laryngeal/pharyngeal squamous lesions with confidence score
studies.humans: Eight pathologists of varying background and experience
studies.finding: Eight pathologists diagnosed and graded squamous dysplasia and carcinoma on 115 slides with and without AI. Inter-rater agreement improved from linear kappa 0.675 without assistance to 0.73 with assistance (p < 0.001), and on high-confidence predictions from 0.731 to 0.809 (p = 0.018).
studies.limitation: Preprint; small reader panel and slide set, outcome is agreement rather than accuracy.
studies.title: Evaluating AI-Assistance for Pathologists in Diagnosing and Grading Laryngeal Lesions

studies.design: Model development with external validation and randomized blinded expert evaluation of AI vs expert segmentations
studies.ai_system: Stepwise transfer learning deep learning segmentation model
studies.humans: Three expert clinicians (pediatric neuroradiologists and radiation oncologists)
studies.finding: Pediatric low-grade glioma MRI segmentations from AI and experts were compared. On external testing AI accuracy was comparable to inter-expert agreement (median DSC 0.834 vs. 0.861, p=0.13), and in blinded rating AI segmentations had higher overall acceptability than experts on average (80.2% vs. 65.4%).
studies.limitation: Preprint; only three expert raters and limited datasets.
studies.title: Expert-level pediatric brain tumor segmentation in a limited data scenario with stepwise transfer learning

studies.design: Vignette comparison of GPT-3 against practicing physicians and lay people on 48 validated case vignettes
studies.humans: Practicing physicians (and a nationally representative sample of lay people)
studies.finding: On 48 validated vignettes, GPT-3 had the correct diagnosis in its top 3 for 88% (95% CI, 75% to 94%) of cases versus 96% (95% CI, 94% to 97%) for physicians (p=0.0354) and 54% for lay individuals. GPT-3 triaged 71% correctly versus 91% (95% CI, 89% to 93%) for physicians (p<0.001).
studies.limitation: Preprint, not peer reviewed; short simplified vignettes (<60 words) rather than real patients; number of physicians not stated.
studies.title: The Diagnostic and Triage Accuracy of the GPT-3 Artificial Intelligence Model

studies.design: Retrospective multi-institution model development with comparison to trainee radiologist segmentations on CT
studies.ai_system: Deep learning segmentation model for ovarian cancer lesions on CT
studies.humans: Trainee radiologist(s) with three years of experience
