studies.finding: For segmentation of pelvic/ovarian and omental ovarian cancer lesions on CT, the model did not perform significantly different from a trainee radiologist for pelvic/ovarian lesions (p=0.392). On the independent test set (n=71) the model achieved 72±19 mean DSC for pelvic/ovarian and 64±24 for omental lesions.
studies.limitation: Preprint, not peer reviewed; comparison only against trainee segmentations, with number of readers not stated and comparison reported only for pelvic/ovarian lesions.
studies.title: Deep learning-based Segmentation of Multi-site Disease in Ovarian Cancer

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on 30 published neuroradiology case conference cases
studies.humans: Three radiologists (junior resident, senior resident, board-certified radiologist)
studies.finding: Diagnosis from medical history and imaging findings in 30 challenging neuroradiology cases. ChatGPT achieved 23% (7/30) accuracy versus 27% (8/30), 30% (9/30) and 47% (14/30) for the junior resident, senior resident and board-certified radiologist. Differences were not significant (p = 0.99, 0.77, and 0.10).
studies.limitation: Only 30 published cases and three readers; preprint not peer reviewed.
studies.title: Comparison of the Diagnostic Performance from Patient's Medical History and Imaging Findings between GPT-4 based ChatGPT and Radiologists in Challenging Neuroradiology Cases

studies.design: Cross-sectional reader study, without then with AI after 3-week washout
studies.finding: Grading 265 fundus photographs for diabetic retinopathy. There was no significant difference without versus with AI in five-class grading (QWK differences +0.010-0.017, p=0.09-0.32), though intergrader agreement increased with AI (FK +0.072, p=0.0003).
studies.limitation: Only four residents at a single centre using a public dataset; preprint not peer reviewed.
studies.title: Impact of an Artificial Intelligence Algorithm on Diabetic Retinopathy Grading by Ophthalmology Residents

studies.design: Blinded comparison of written answers to 15 vestibular schwannoma questions from GPT models versus neurosurgeons, rated by three experienced neurosurgeons
studies.humans: Four neurosurgeons answering; three experienced neurosurgeons rating
studies.finding: On 15 clinical and surgical questions on vestibular schwannoma, both GPT models answered faster than expert neurosurgeons (p<0.01). Their responses were consistently non-inferior in accuracy, coherence, relevance, thoroughness and overall performance, and often rated higher than expert responses; context enrichment did not significantly change speed or performance (p>0.999).
studies.limitation: Preprint; only 15 questions and four neurosurgeon respondents, with subjective ratings.
studies.title: neuroGPT-X: Towards an Accountable Expert Opinion Tool for Vestibular Schwannoma

studies.design: Multi-site analytical and clinical validation comparing assisted and unassisted pathologist reads
studies.finding: Histology scoring of MASH liver biopsies. AIM-NASH-assisted reads were superior to unassisted reads for inflammation, ballooning, NAS >= 4 with >=1 in each category, and MASH resolution, and non-inferior for steatosis and fibrosis.
studies.limitation: Preprint; abstract gives no numbers or reader count.
studies.title: Analytical and Clinical Validation of AIM-NASH: A Digital Pathology Tool for Artificial Intelligence-based Measurement of Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis Histology

studies.design: Pragmatic single-system randomised controlled trial over 90 days
studies.ai_system: Epic EHR-integrated generative AI chart summarization tool
studies.finding: Clinicians were randomised to the AI chart summarization tool or usual care. Physician task load favored the intervention (-27.4; 95% CI, -49.4 to -5.3; P=0.02), with lower burnout (-0.20) but no significant difference in charting time per encounter (-1.2 seconds; 95% CI, -19.0 to 16.6).
studies.limitation: Preprint; single academic health system with declining engagement and mainly self-reported outcomes.
studies.title: A Pragmatic Randomized Trial of an EHR-Integrated Generative AI Chart Summarization Tool for Ambulatory Clinicians

studies.design: Prospective randomized trial of standard ophthalmology notes with vs without LLM plain language summaries
studies.finding: Non-ophthalmology providers given notes with a plain language summary reported enhanced diagnostic understanding (p=0.012) and improved explanation clarity (p<0.001), and 85% preferred the summary. Summary error rate was 26% on initial ophthalmologist review and 15% on over-read.
studies.limitation: Preprint; outcomes are self-reported comprehension with 33% response rate.
studies.title: Utilizing AI-Generated Plain Language Summaries to Enhance Interdisciplinary Understanding of Ophthalmology Notes: A Randomized Trial

studies.design: Randomised trial of LLM-drafted versus template-assembled paediatric ED discharge documents, clinician-validated
studies.humans: Discharging clinicians in a paediatric emergency department
studies.finding: Among 117 analysed children, record-concordant family understanding at follow-up did not differ between LLM-assisted and conventional documents (difference -0.01; 95% CI -0.12 to 0.10); no seriously consequential discrepancy occurred (0/117). Clinicians edited 48 of 58 drafts, removing 18 of 22 unsupported additions but only 6 of 22 incorrect abbreviation expansions.
studies.limitation: Small sample with attrition (117 of 153 analysed), single centre; oversight findings exploratory; preprint.
studies.title: From clinician review to measurable human oversight of AI-drafted paediatric discharge documents

studies.design: Quasi-experimental interrupted time-series
studies.humans: Primary care physicians and advanced practice providers
studies.finding: Documentation burden before vs after AI scribe adoption over 150 days. Note writing time decreased 7% at day zero (IRR 0.93) and 16% by day 150 (IRR 0.84); at day 150 pajama time fell 19%, TOSH 13%, and wRVU rose 2%; note length unchanged.
studies.limitation: Preprint; non-randomised pre-post design without concurrent control.
studies.title: Longitudinal effects ambient AI scribe use on documentation burden and financial productivity: A quasi-experimental study

studies.design: Within-subject pre-post evaluation in an NHS ambulance service
studies.ai_system: Ambient voice technology with generative AI
studies.finding: Assessment and documentation with AVT vs baseline. Hear and Treat assessments shortened (15 vs 17 minutes) and throughput rose 15% (2.3 vs 2.0 patients/hour) without compromising documentation quality; on-scene time fell from 44 to 41 minutes (-6.8%).
studies.limitation: Preprint, uncontrolled pre-post design without randomisation.
studies.title: 'What witchcraft is this?': Paramedics report gains in productivity, well-being, and patient flow from piloting ambient voice technology in an NHS Ambulance Service

studies.design: Prospective cross-over within-subject simulation study
studies.finding: Clinicians documented simulated psychiatric consultations with keyboard versus an ambient AI scribe. Documentation quality (SAIL) was 22.88 with AI versus 14.38 without (p=0.038), and NASA-TLX workload was 25.0 versus 461.3 (p<0.001); screen time 7.46 versus 5.31 minutes was not significantly different (p=0.27).
studies.limitation: Only eight clinicians in a simulated setting; preprint, not peer reviewed.
studies.title: Evaluating an Ambient Artificial Intelligence Scribe for Documentation Quality and Efficiency in Psychiatric Consultations: A Simulation-based Study

studies.design: Blinded within-subject comparison of paired LLM- and physician-authored ED one-liner summaries for 99 encounters, rated by emergency physicians
studies.humans: Emergency physicians (authors of original summaries); 21 emergency physician raters
studies.finding: Twenty-one emergency physicians rated LLM- and physician-authored one-liner summaries for 99 ED encounters. LLM summaries scored higher for accuracy (4.18 vs 3.40), completeness (3.69 vs 3.25) and clinical utility (3.88 vs 3.21). LLM summaries were preferred in 50.5% of encounters, physician summaries in 38.4%, and 11.1% rated equivalent.
studies.limitation: Single-centre preprint with subjective Likert ratings of 99 encounters; physician summaries were written in routine practice, not under study conditions.
studies.title: Physician- versus Large Language Model-Generated Clinical Summaries in the Emergency Department

studies.design: Single-centre blinded comparison of AI agent versus physician readmission reviews on 20 readmissions
studies.ai_system: Agentic AI workflow using a large language model
studies.finding: For 30-day readmission review, blinded overall quality ratings were similar for AI and physician reviews (4.35 vs. 4.20 on a 1-5 scale; mean difference 0.15, 95% CI -0.20 to 0.48; p=0.49). AI classified 9/20 readmissions (45%) as preventable versus 19/40 physician reviews (47.5%).
studies.limitation: Preprint; very small single-centre sample of 20 readmissions.
studies.title: Agentic Artificial Intelligence for Hospital Readmission Review: A Single-Center Blinded Evaluation and Exploratory Qualitative Analysis

studies.design: Single-site blinded counterbalanced crossover non-inferiority evaluation
studies.finding: Three raters scored AI-generated and manual summaries of 37 paediatric cancer genomics reports on the Quality Summary Index. Mean content scores were 4.01 vs 3.97 and presentation scores 4.39 vs 4.12 for AI vs manual; non-inferiority was demonstrated for both co-primary endpoints.
studies.limitation: Preprint; small single-site sample with only three raters and low inter-rater reliability.
studies.title: Evaluation of AI-assisted summarisation of tertiary clinical genomics reports: results of the QNOMX-VHIR-CPSP-001 Phase 1 study

studies.design: Model development with blinded reader rating study
studies.finding: Free-text 12-lead ECG reports rated by cardiologists and residents. Paired win-tie-loss distribution was 32:35:33 and forced-choice preference 0.53, with no significant difference between model and reference clinician reports.
studies.limitation: Preprint; number of raters not stated; comparison against reference reports rather than live clinicians.
studies.title: A unified 12-lead ECG-language model for interpretation and clinical-endpoint prediction

studies.design: Mixed-methods evaluation of physicians answering patient-specific questions with LLM summaries versus standard chart review
studies.finding: Physicians answered clinical questions about heart failure admissions using LLM-generated summaries or standard chart review. Accuracy was 88.0% with summaries versus 86.4% without, and summary access did not significantly reduce overall completion time, though frequent summary use was associated with faster completion (p = 0.002).
studies.limitation: Preprint; number of physicians not reported and the evaluation was a questionnaire task rather than live care.
studies.title: Verifiable Summarization of Electronic Health Records Using Large Language Models to Support Chart Review

studies.design: Case-control analysis of EHR notes
studies.finding: Among 20,302 matched primary care annual visit notes, ambient-scribed notes had significantly greater neuropsychiatric symptom documentation in all 6 RDoC domains (p <.001). Likelihood of psychiatric intervention was lower for ambient-scribed vs unscribed visits (aOR 0.83, 95% CI 0.72-0.95), but not for human-scribed vs unscribed (aOR 1.01, 95% CI 0.87-1.17).
studies.limitation: Preprint; observational case-control design with LLM-estimated symptom documentation, so causation cannot be inferred.
studies.title: Changes in psychiatric documentation and treatment in primary care with artificial intelligence scribe use

studies.design: Blinded expert evaluation of AI vs human-written discharge summaries
studies.humans: Physicians who wrote actual discharge summaries; Internal Medicine faculty raters
studies.finding: Internal Medicine faculty scored AI-generated and actual human-written inpatient discharge summaries. AI summaries significantly outperformed human-written summaries in quality and readability/conciseness and were comparable in factuality and completeness.
studies.limitation: Preprint; sample size and number of raters not stated in abstract.
studies.title: Towards Inpatient Discharge Summary Automation via Large Language Models: A Multidimensional Evaluation with a HIPAA-Compliant Instance of GPT-4o and Clinical Expert Assessment

studies.design: Blinded comparison of AI vs clinician post-discharge synopses
studies.finding: AI and clinicians summarized 80 de-identified recently hospitalized patients, rated blind by physicians. AI synopses were rated useful 75% of the time versus 76% for human ones; AI had lower succinctness for the Data task (55-67% vs 84-86%).
studies.limitation: Small de-identified dataset; number of clinicians not stated; preprint.
studies.title: Can Electronic care planning using AI Summarization Yield equal Documentation Quality? (EASY eDocQ)

studies.design: Retrospective blinded comparison of GPT-4 vs physician-written ED discharge letters
studies.finding: Across 72 discharge letters, evaluators preferred GPT-4 letters in 1,009 of 1,206 evaluations (83.7%), with higher empathy, clarity and overall quality ratings (p < 0.001). GPT-4 letters had median medical accuracy 5.0 vs 4.0 for physician letters (p = 0.025).
studies.limitation: Preprint; small sample of 72 letters with subjective ratings; number of authoring physicians not stated.
studies.title: Empathy and clarity in GPT-4-Generated Emergency Department Discharge Letters

studies.design: Multi-country paired simulation study
studies.finding: In 385 actor-performed consultations across five countries, an AI scribe and a clinician each wrote a note. AI notes scored higher on PDQI-9 (40.6 vs 35.6; difference +5.08, 95% CI 4.6-5.6). Clinician notes more often carried ≥1 Critical+High error: 61.0% versus 24.4% by the calibrated reviewer (RR 2.50) and 21.8% versus 6.2% by clinician adjudication (RR 3.50).
studies.limitation: Preprint; simulated consultations with junior clinicians and unedited AI notes, not live practice.
studies.title: Quality, consistency, and clinical safety of AI-generated versus clinician-written clinical notes: a multi-country paired simulation study

studies.design: Blinded comparison of AI vs clinician summaries of simulated EHRs
studies.finding: Clinicians and ChatGPT-4 summarised 70 simulated primary care EHRs, rated blind by clinicians. Clinician-authored summaries were rated higher overall (7.39 versus 7.00 out of 10; p=0.02), with similar accuracy, and AI summaries were less likely to omit important information.
studies.limitation: Simulated records; small number of clinicians; preprint.
studies.title: Comparing AI- versus clinician-authored summaries of simulated primary care electronic health records

studies.design: Comparison of LLMs with medical student cohort on a university progress test
studies.humans: 1057 University of Toronto undergraduate medical students
studies.finding: On a 100-question undergraduate medical progress test, ChatGPT answered 68.0% and GPT-4 79.0% correctly, versus student means of 36.3% (Year 1) to 58.5% (Year 4). GPT-4 performed at a level equivalent to the top performing student.
studies.limitation: Preprint; single 100-question exam with students, not practising physicians.
studies.title: Comparing the Performance of ChatGPT and GPT-4 versus a Cohort of Medical Students on an Official University of Toronto Undergraduate Medical Education Progress Test

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on 30 board-style questions
studies.finding: 30 otolaryngology board-style questions. ChatGPT outperformed MS1, MS2 and MS3 (p = <0.001, 0.003, 0.019), while PGY4 and PGY5 residents outperformed ChatGPT (p = 0.033 and 0.002); no statistical difference for MS4 and PGY1-3.
studies.limitation: Preprint; only 30 exam questions testing recall, small trainee sample.
studies.title: Is ChatGPT smarter than Otolaryngology trainees? A comparison study of board style exam questions

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on 331 in-service exam questions
studies.humans: Second-year periodontics residents across the US (benchmark scores)
studies.finding: 2024 periodontology in-service examination (331 MCQs). ChatGPT-4o, Gemini Advanced and Claude 3 Opus scored 92.7, 81.6 and 78.5 percent respectively, compared with the residents' 61.9 percent.
studies.limitation: Preprint; exam questions only, residents' aggregate benchmark used.
studies.title: Artificial Intelligence in Periodontology: Performance Evaluation of ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini on the In-service Examination

studies.design: Comparison on ASCP Resident Question Bank practice tests against average peer performance
studies.finding: ChatGPT answered text-only ASCP Resident Question Bank 2022 pathology questions. Its overall performance was 56.98%, lower than the average peer performance of 62.81%.
studies.limitation: Preprint; image questions excluded and peer comparison based on aggregate question-bank averages.
studies.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT's Pathology Knowledge using Board-Style Questions

studies.design: Cross-sectional comparison on 1440 exam questions from six TUS examinations
studies.humans: Physicians taking the Turkish Medical Specialization Exam
studies.finding: Answering Turkish Medical Specialization Exam questions. GPT-4 achieved a success rate of 70.56% versus 40.17% for GPT-3.5 and 38.14% for physicians, though doctors outperformed AI on anatomy.
studies.limitation: Exam questions only, with no reported number of physicians; preprint not peer reviewed.
studies.title: AI in Medical Education: A Comparative Analysis of GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 on Turkish Medical Specialization Exam Performance

studies.design: Single-blind randomized clinical trial
studies.finding: Physicians diagnosed 6 vignettes with voluntary access to ChatGPT-4o advice that was either error-free or contained errors in 3 of 6 cases. Diagnostic reasoning accuracy was 84.9% with error-free versus 73.3% with flawed recommendations (adjusted difference -14.0 percentage points). Top-choice diagnosis accuracy was 90.5% versus 76.1% (adjusted difference -18.3 percentage points).
studies.limitation: Preprint; small sample of 44 physicians and only 6 vignettes, with no no-AI control arm.
studies.title: Automation Bias in Large Language Model Assisted Diagnostic Reasoning Among AI-Trained Physicians
studies.excluded: preprint of S6 (Automation Bias in LLM-Assisted Diagnostic Reasoning among AI-trained physicians), already in the paper (editor, 2026-11-08)

studies.design: Multi-institutional randomized controlled trial with five clinical vignettes
studies.humans: Attending physicians and residents in internal, family or emergency medicine
studies.finding: Open-ended management reasoning on expert-developed vignettes. Physicians using GPT-4 scored higher than those using conventional resources (mean difference 6.5%, 95% CI 2.7-10.2, p<0.001) and spent more time per case (119.3 seconds). There was no significant difference between GPT-4-augmented physicians and GPT-4 alone (-0.9%, 95% CI -9.0 to 7.2, p=0.8).
studies.limitation: Preprint; simulated vignettes rather than live patient care.
studies.title: Large Language Model Influence on Management Reasoning: A Randomized Controlled Trial
studies.excluded: preprint of S33 (GPT-4 assistance for physician performance on patient care tasks, Nature Medicine 2025), already in the paper (editor, 2026-11-08)
